knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8,
                      fig.height = 4.2, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(amorem)

# Case study: Social Evolution

The Social Evolution study (Madan et al. 2011) recorded phone calls among
undergraduates in an MIT residence hall, together with each student's floor and
grade and two waves of a friendship survey. This page models who calls whom from
three kinds of information:

- the calling history itself (endogenous statistics),
- actor attributes shared by caller and callee (homophily),
- friendship nominations reported in the survey before the call.

The code runs when this page is built.

## Data intake

```{r intake}
data(social_evolution_calls)
data(social_evolution_actors)
data(social_evolution_friendship)

calls <- standardize_event_log(social_evolution_calls, drop_loops = TRUE)
c(calls = nrow(calls), callers = length(unique(c(calls$sender, calls$receiver))),
  days = max(calls$time))
head(social_evolution_actors)
table(social_evolution_friendship$time)
```

`standardize_event_log()` checks and sorts the log: it removes loops, rows with
missing values and duplicated `(sender, receiver, time)` triples, of which this
log has `r nrow(social_evolution_calls) - nrow(calls)`. The
`r nrow(calls)` calls involve `r length(unique(c(calls$sender, calls$receiver)))`
of the `r nrow(social_evolution_actors)` students in the actor table. In that
table `r sum(social_evolution_actors$present)` of the
`r nrow(social_evolution_actors)` students are recorded as present, so no dyad
has to be removed from the risk set for absence. The risk set below is the set of
dyads among the students who appear in the calls.

The friendship survey has two waves, on day
`r fmt(min(social_evolution_friendship$time))` and day
`r fmt(max(social_evolution_friendship$time))`. The second wave comes after the
last call (day `r fmt(max(calls$time))`), so only the first wave can inform a
call.

```{r networks, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 5.4, fig.alt = "The call network and the first-wave friendship network drawn on one layout, students coloured by floor"}
fr1 <- social_evolution_friendship[social_evolution_friendship$time == min(social_evolution_friendship$time) &
                                     social_evolution_friendship$replace == 1, ]
cw <- aggregate(list(w = rep(1, nrow(calls))), list(from = calls$sender, to = calls$receiver), sum)
fw <- data.frame(from = fr1$sender, to = fr1$receiver, w = 1)
ids <- unique(c(cw$from, cw$to, fw$from, fw$to))
lay <- withr::with_preserve_seed(layout_graph(rbind(cw, fw), ids = ids, seed = 3))
floor_of <- setNames(social_evolution_actors$floor, social_evolution_actors$id)
floor_col <- setNames(pal[1:9], 1:9)
nodes <- data.frame(id = lay$id, x = lay$x, y = lay$y, size = 1,
                    col = floor_col[as.character(floor_of[lay$id])], label = NA)
same_floor_col <- function(e) ifelse(floor_of[e$from] == floor_of[e$to], floor_col[as.character(floor_of[e$from])], "#B4BBC0")
layout(matrix(c(1, 2, 3, 3), 2, byrow = TRUE), heights = c(6, 1))
par(mar = c(0.3, 0.3, 3, 0.3))
draw_network(transform(nodes, size = as.numeric(table(factor(c(calls$sender, calls$receiver), levels = id)))),
             transform(cw, col = same_floor_col(cw)), directed = TRUE, max_lwd = 3.5, node_scale = c(0.9, 2.8))
title_left(sprintf("Calls: %d calls on %d pairs", nrow(calls), nrow(cw)),
           sprintf("%s%% of calls stay within a floor  \u00b7  arrow: caller to callee", fmt(100 * mean(floor_of[calls$sender] == floor_of[calls$receiver], na.rm = TRUE), 0)))
draw_network(transform(nodes, size = as.numeric(table(factor(c(fw$from, fw$to), levels = id)))),
             transform(fw, col = same_floor_col(fw)), directed = TRUE, max_lwd = 1, node_scale = c(0.9, 2.8))
title_left(sprintf("Friendship survey, first wave: %d nominations", nrow(fw)),
           sprintf("%s%% of nominations stay within a floor  \u00b7  same layout as the calls", fmt(100 * mean(floor_of[fw$from] == floor_of[fw$to], na.rm = TRUE), 0)))
par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0)); plot.new()
legend("center", legend = paste("floor", 1:9), pt.bg = floor_col, col = "white", pch = 21, pt.cex = 1.6,
       bty = "n", horiz = TRUE, cex = 0.72, text.col = ink, title = "colour: the student's floor; grey lines join students of different floors",
       title.col = ink_soft)
```

```{r networks-numbers, include = FALSE}
call_floor <- mean(floor_of[calls$sender] == floor_of[calls$receiver], na.rm = TRUE)
fr_floor <- mean(floor_of[fw$from] == floor_of[fw$to], na.rm = TRUE)
```

Both networks are drawn on one layout computed from the calls and the
nominations together, so a student sits in the same place in the two panels.
`r fmt(100 * call_floor, 0)`% of the calls and `r fmt(100 * fr_floor, 0)`% of
the first-wave nominations join two students of the same floor.

## Case-control sample and covariates

Each call is matched with five non-events, dyads drawn uniformly among the
students who appear in the calls (`sample_non_events()` with its defaults,
`scope = "all"` and `mode = "one"`).
Endogenous statistics are computed against the history of calls only (the
sampled non-events never enter it). The time since the dyad's last call is
mapped to a weight in (0, 1] with `transform_recency()`, with weight 0 for a
dyad that has not called before.

```{r case-control}
cc <- sample_non_events(calls, n_controls = 5, seed = 2008)
cc <- endogenous_features(cc, stats = c("recency", "reciprocity_binary",
                                        "sender_outdegree", "receiver_indegree"))
cc$recency_w <- transform_recency(cc$recency)
cc$recency_w[is.na(cc$recency_w)] <- 0
for (s in c("reciprocity_binary", "sender_outdegree", "receiver_indegree")) {
  cc[[s]][is.na(cc[[s]])] <- 0
}
```

Actor attributes are attached to both ends of every row with
`attach_static_covariates()` and turned into homophily indicators. Students with
no recorded grade do not count as sharing a grade.

```{r attributes}
actors <- social_evolution_actors[, c("id", "floor", "gradeType")]
cc <- attach_static_covariates(cc, sender_covariates = actors,
                               receiver_covariates = actors, actor_col = "id")
cc$same_floor <- as.integer(cc$sender_floor == cc$receiver_floor)
cc$same_grade <- as.integer(!is.na(cc$sender_gradeType) &
                            !is.na(cc$receiver_gradeType) &
                            cc$sender_gradeType == cc$receiver_gradeType)
```

Friendship is a time-varying dyadic covariate: for each row, the latest survey
record for the dyad with a time strictly before the row's time.
`friend` is the caller's nomination of the callee, `friend_back` the callee's
nomination of the caller.

```{r friendship}
fr <- social_evolution_friendship
friend_at <- function(s, r, t) {
  k <- fr$sender == s & fr$receiver == r & fr$time < t
  if (!any(k)) 0L else fr$replace[k][which.max(fr$time[k])]
}
cc$friend      <- mapply(friend_at, cc$sender,   cc$receiver, cc$time)
cc$friend_back <- mapply(friend_at, cc$receiver, cc$sender,   cc$time)

prop <- function(v) tapply(cc[[v]], cc$event, mean)
rbind(friend = prop("friend"), same_floor = prop("same_floor"),
      same_grade = prop("same_grade"))   # columns: controls (0), calls (1)
```

```{r shares, include = FALSE}
pf <- prop("friend"); pfl <- prop("same_floor")
```

`r fmt(100 * pf[["1"]], 0)`% of calls go to a student the caller had nominated
as a friend, against `r fmt(100 * pf[["0"]], 0)`% of sampled non-events;
`r fmt(100 * pfl[["1"]], 0)`% of calls and `r fmt(100 * pfl[["0"]], 0)`% of
non-events stay on the caller's floor.

## Conditional logistic regression

`rem(method = "clogit")` fits the case-5-control design. Four specifications
share the same sample:

```{r clogit}
specs <- list(
  endogenous = event ~ recency_w + reciprocity_binary + sender_outdegree +
                       receiver_indegree,
  homophily  = event ~ recency_w + reciprocity_binary + sender_outdegree +
                       receiver_indegree + same_floor + same_grade,
  friendship = event ~ recency_w + reciprocity_binary + sender_outdegree +
                       receiver_indegree + friend + friend_back,
  full       = event ~ recency_w + reciprocity_binary + sender_outdegree +
                       receiver_indegree + same_floor + same_grade +
                       friend + friend_back)
fits <- lapply(specs, rem, data = cc, method = "clogit", stratum = "stratum")
aic <- sapply(fits, function(f) stats::AIC(logLik(f)))
data.frame(AIC = round(aic, 1), delta_AIC = round(aic - min(aic), 1))
```

```{r clogit-numbers, include = FALSE}
best <- names(which.min(aic))
ct <- summary(fits$full$fit)$coefficients
hr <- function(v) fmt(exp(ct[v, "coef"]))
ci <- function(v) paste(fmt(exp(ct[v, "coef"] - 1.96 * ct[v, "se(coef)"])),
                        fmt(exp(ct[v, "coef"] + 1.96 * ct[v, "se(coef)"])), sep = "–")
```

The `r best` specification has the lowest AIC. Adding friendship to the
endogenous model lowers the AIC by `r fmt(aic[["endogenous"]] - aic[["friendship"]], 1)`;
adding the two homophily indicators lowers it by
`r fmt(aic[["endogenous"]] - aic[["homophily"]], 1)`.

```{r clogit-figure, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 3.4, fig.alt = "Log hazard ratios of the full conditional logistic model with 95% intervals"}
term_label <- c(recency_w = "recency weight", reciprocity_binary = "reply to an earlier call",
                sender_outdegree = "caller's earlier calls", receiver_indegree = "callee's calls received",
                same_floor = "same floor", same_grade = "same grade",
                friend = "caller nominated callee", friend_back = "callee nominated caller")
forest(ct[, "coef"], ct[, "se(coef)"], labels = term_label[rownames(ct)],
       xlab = "log hazard ratio, 95% interval (full model)")
```

The recency weight runs from 0 (no earlier call on the dyad) to 1 (a call
just before), so its coefficient compares those two extremes: hazard ratio
`r fmt(exp(ct["recency_w", "coef"]), 0)` (95% interval `r ci("recency_w")`),
which sets the scale of the figure. In the full model, a call to a nominated
friend has hazard ratio
`r hr("friend")` (95% interval `r ci("friend")`), and a call that reciprocates an
earlier call in the other direction `r hr("reciprocity_binary")`
(`r ci("reciprocity_binary")`). The interval for `same_floor` is
`r ci("same_floor")` and for `same_grade` `r ci("same_grade")`.

## Sender random effect

Some students call far more than others. A sender random effect absorbs these
differences without a statistic for them. The `re()` term needs the one-control
(degenerate logistic) design of `rem(method = "gam")`, so a case-1-control
sample is drawn and widened with `widen_case_control()`, which keeps the
sender of each call and of its control (`sender_ev`, `sender_nv`).

```{r gam-data}
cc1 <- sample_non_events(calls, n_controls = 1, seed = 2008)
cc1 <- endogenous_features(cc1, stats = "sender_outdegree")
cc1$sender_outdegree[is.na(cc1$sender_outdegree)] <- 0
cc1 <- attach_static_covariates(cc1, sender_covariates = actors,
                                receiver_covariates = actors, actor_col = "id")
cc1$same_floor <- as.integer(cc1$sender_floor == cc1$receiver_floor)
cc1$friend <- mapply(friend_at, cc1$sender, cc1$receiver, cc1$time)
w <- widen_case_control(cc1, covariates = c("same_floor", "friend",
                                            "sender_outdegree"))
```

With a single control per call, the history statistics separate calls from
controls almost perfectly (a sampled dyad has rarely called before), so the
models below use the friendship and floor indicators. The sender effect enters
either as the sender's number of earlier calls or as a random effect:

```{r gam}
g_base <- rem(~ same_floor + friend, data = w, method = "gam", gam_method = "REML")
g_out  <- rem(~ same_floor + friend + sender_outdegree, data = w,
              method = "gam", gam_method = "REML")
g_re   <- rem(~ same_floor + friend + re(sender), data = w,
              method = "gam", gam_method = "REML")
gaic <- c(base = stats::AIC(g_base$fit), outdegree = stats::AIC(g_out$fit),
          random_effect = stats::AIC(g_re$fit))
round(gaic, 1)
summary(g_re)$s.table
```

```{r gam-numbers, include = FALSE}
st <- summary(g_re)$s.table
```

The random effect has `r fmt(st[1, "edf"], 1)` effective degrees of freedom for
`r length(unique(c(w$sender_ev, w$sender_nv)))` senders, and the model with it
has an AIC `r fmt(gaic[["base"]] - gaic[["random_effect"]], 1)` lower than the
model without a sender term and `r fmt(gaic[["outdegree"]] - gaic[["random_effect"]], 1)`
lower than the one with the sender's earlier calls.

```{r re-figure, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 4, fig.alt = "Estimated sender random effects against the number of calls each student made, coloured by floor"}
b <- stats::coef(g_re)
b <- b[grep("RE_sender", names(b))]
lev <- levels(factor(c(w$sender_ev, w$sender_nv)))
n_sent <- table(factor(calls$sender, levels = lev))
op <- par(mar = c(3.6, 4, 3, 7))
plot(as.integer(n_sent) + 1, b, log = "x", type = "n", axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
abline(h = 0, col = rule, lwd = 1.2)
points(as.integer(n_sent) + 1, b, pch = 21, bg = alpha(floor_col[as.character(floor_of[lev])], 0.85),
       col = "white", cex = 1.5)
axis(1, at = c(1, 2, 5, 11, 21, 51, 101), labels = c(0, 1, 4, 10, 20, 50, 100), tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.75,
     col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.5)
axis(2, las = 1, tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.75, col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.5)
mtext("calls made (log scale)", side = 1, line = 2, cex = 0.75, col = ink_soft)
mtext("sender random effect", side = 2, line = 2.4, cex = 0.75, col = ink_soft)
title_left("One point per student", "colour: floor")
legend("right", inset = c(-0.16, 0), xpd = TRUE, legend = paste("floor", 1:9), pt.bg = floor_col, col = "white",
       pch = 21, pt.cex = 1.3, bty = "n", cex = 0.68, text.col = ink)
par(op)
```

```{r re-numbers, include = FALSE}
r_sp <- stats::cor(as.integer(n_sent), b, method = "spearman")
```

Each point is a student. Students who made no calls appear only as senders of
sampled non-events, which places their effects below zero. The Spearman
correlation between a student's random
effect and the number of calls the student made is `r fmt(r_sp)`.

## References

Madan A, Cebrian M, Moturu S, Farrahi K, Pentland A (2011). Sensing the
"health state" of a community. *IEEE Pervasive Computing* 11(1), 36–45.
